sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that recognizing one's lowliness leads one to educate oneself like a child with self-sacrifice, a daily obligation derived from the eternal Torah and the Baal Shem Tov's teaching, especially regarding the education of children.

translations.translation: d)
And behold,
another effect of the aforementioned nullification,

that one who recognizes that he is at the ultimate descent etc. causes him that even if his service is proper, nevertheless he will educate himself in the manner of the education of young children literally,
for he feels himself to be like an infant in his service
(and as above, for what is he considered relative to his true value).
And the matter of education must be with self-sacrifice
(as above),
and as is explained in the aforementioned maamar,
the self-sacrifice that existed in this during the time of Mordechai,
and behold the Torah is eternal,
that in this there is an instruction
[Torah from the term instruction,
as it is brought in the Zohar]
eternal for each and every one in every time and in every place,
that one must give over his soul for the matter of education,
whether for the education of himself,
as the statement of the Mishnah,
"Who is wise? One who learns from every person,"
that this education must be every single day throughout all the days of his life,
for behold, every day he must ascend in his service, as the statement,
"We ascend in holiness,"
that even when he is in the category of holy,
for "holy" is a word in and of itself,
it is the category of wisdom
[which is in the level of wise, for yesterday he already learned from every person],
behold even then there must be an ascent,
that when a new day arrives, "he does his work"
and adds to learn from every person and rises in his level of wisdom,
meaning that every single day there must be the education of himself.
And so too is understood from the well-known teaching of the Baal Shem Tov,
that in every matter that a Jew sees or hears, he must see and hear
(perceive and overhear)
the instruction within it for his service to his Master,
meaning that in every matter he sees or hears, he must educate himself.
And all the more so must one give over his soul for the matter of the education of young children literally.
And especially there is in this an obligation upon the young men and young women, as my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, adds in his letter in connection with his aforementioned maamar,
that the times demand,
that each and every one of the young men and young women, may they live,
behold not only that they themselves, in their private lives,
must be firm and strong in the observance of the practical mitzvos in all their beauty etc.
[and through this be a living example]
but furthermore,
[and this too is essential]
to make an environment of Torah learners and mitzvah observers,
to the extent that they will see among them openly that they are "a planting of My planting, the work of My hands, to be glorified."
And in general,
this obligation is upon each and every one,
for each and every one is included in "young men and young women" when it is recalled that every single day he becomes a new creation.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through the education of young children, "from the mouths of babes and sucklings You have established strength" to silence the enemy and avenger, which correspond to revealed and hidden evil overcome by the work of "my sword and my bow."

translations.translation: And behold, through the education of young children, "from the mouths of babes and sucklings You have established strength... to silence the enemy and the avenger,"
and as is explained in the aforementioned maamar,
that the enemy is the revealed hater,
and the avenger is a hidden hater who invents pretexts etc.
[And in the service, this is the matter of what Yaakov said,
"which I took from the hand of the Emorite with my sword and with my bow,"
for the difference between a sword and a bow is that the sword kills the hater who stands near him, close by,
and the bow can also kill the hater who stands from afar,
for the close hater refers to
(coarseness)
the evil that a person knows and understands is evil,
and the hater who stands from afar is the subtlety of evil that he does not know about etc.
And the removal of the enemy and avenger is through the work of "my sword and my bow,"
as is explained in the maamarim
regarding the matter of the five weapons enumerated in the Mishnah of Shabbos.]

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the power for this service comes from Moshe Rabbeinu, whose aspect in every Jew connects the soul's root to the embodied soul, enabling the crushing of descent to become a light reaching the light itself.

translations.translation: e)
And behold, the power for the aforementioned service is through Moshe Rabbeinu.
As is explained in the aforementioned maamar,
that this is the meaning of "And you shall command the children of Israel etc.,"
for "tetzaveh" is a term of connection and bonding,
and "you" refers
(in the simple meaning of the verse)
to Moshe,
and the extension of Moshe in every generation,
that in each one of Israel there is something of the aspect of Moshe, as it is brought in Tikkunei Zohar
and cited in Igeres HaKodesh of the Alter Rebbe,
and in each one, behold the aspect of Moshe within him is revealed to the extent that "even a trivial matter" is
"small" relative to it, as it is brought in Tanya, Part One,
and the aspect of Moshe within each one of Israel connects in a manner of connection and bonding
(tetzaveh)
the
root of the soul
to the soul that is clothed in the body, together with the animal soul and his body and his portion in the world,
and gives power that it should be "crushed for light,"
that from this being crushed and broken due to the descent of the soul into this lowly world, below which there is no lower,
which is a tremendous descent,
for even when this world is at its ultimate perfection it is called a "deep pit,"
from which it is understood that the very fact that the soul descended into this world is a great descent.
And due to the descent,
even if he is in a state of ultimate expansion in physicality and also in spirituality, nevertheless, what is he considered relative to his true standing and state
(before the descent)
which is in the category of "son,"
the only one of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He,
(as is known the parable regarding this in the maamar of 5666),
behold from the crushing
(that is broken and crushed)
it becomes a light that reaches the light itself, as above.
